title: Journey
description: A goal expressed as an ordered walk over transitions, plus the assertions that prove the goal was reached. The order and the point of a walk live here and nowhere else: transitions[] is a set, and a set has neither.

goal.description: Business outcome in one sentence: 'Complete a purchase using a valid coupon'. NEVER the raw instruction when the instruction carried a credential: the instruction is an input to the model, not part of it, and a journey is copied into test headers and reports. Record the goal, not the sentence that produced it.

goal_stated.description: True when an actor actually asked for this outcome; false when the tools derived the walk and this is the closest honest reading of it. A derived journey is still a valid journey, but a reader must be able to tell the two apart without consulting metadata - 'we were asked to do this' and 'this is the only thing we did' are different claims.

actor.description: Role the journey is exercised as. Must equal an application.actors[].id.

start_state.description: State the journey assumes as a starting point. Derived from the first transition when omitted.

steps.description: The ordered walk. Steps reference top-level transitions rather than restating them, so the edge stays the single place that says what a behaviour does between two surfaces, and the walk stays the single place that says in what order and to what end.

assertions.description: What must be true for the journey to count as passed.

criticality.description: Test selection hint: smoke/critical run on every PR, extended runs nightly.

variants.description: Named data variations of the same journey (valid coupon, expired coupon, coupon over threshold).

argument_overrides.description: Step index (as a string) or transition id -> concrete argument values for this variant.

expected.description: Expected outcome for this variant: a state id (state_checkout), an error code, or a message. Free-form on purpose, because a rejected variant ends somewhere the graph may not model yet.

journeyStep.description: One turn of the walk: take this edge, with these argument bindings. Deliberately thin - anything a step could restate about the edge (from_state, to_state, behaviour, effects) already lives on the edge, and a second place to say it is a second place to disagree with it.

arguments.description: Argument bindings for this walk, overriding the edge's own recorded values where the walk used different ones. Keys must be the behaviour's declared input names.
